boundary_rationale: A prose-sermon superscription opens the unit, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), matching “The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.30.1) — the hadavar-asher-hayah shape that opens the consolation core's own parent frame. A command to write follows without any change of speaker, כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּתָב לְךָ֗ אֵ֧ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֶל סֵֽפֶר (oshb:Jer.30.2, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.” (web:Jer.30.2) — write every word spoken into a book. The content commanded to be written follows at once, closing on the promise itself: כִּ֠י הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְ֠שַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁב֨וּת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֗ים אֶל הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם וִֽירֵשֽׁוּהָ (oshb:Jer.30.3, byte), matching “For, behold, the days come,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will reverse the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.’” (web:Jer.30.3). A third-person rubric then names what has just been given, וְאֵ֣לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְאֶל יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte), matching “These are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.” (web:Jer.30.4) — dropping out of quoted divine speech into the narrator's own summary of it. Nothing between the header and this rubric reopens the address with a new addressee or discourse imperative, so the whole four-verse frame stands as one unit. A fresh koh-amar opens the first poem at verse 5, matching “For Yahweh says: ” (web:Jer.30.5), and this row stops short of that onset.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 4's shift from quoted divine speech into third-person rubric was considered, since the mode plainly changes there; it is rejected because no addressee shift, koh-amar onset, or discourse imperative marks that specific turn, and the rubric functions as this same frame's own closing heading rather than an independent unit.

boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens the unit, כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte), matching “We have heard a voice of trembling; a voice of fear, and not of peace.” (web:Jer.30.5) — a communal cry of dread rather than a report about a third party. The day named next carries the hoy interjection in its own DAY-ALAS shape, not a woe-oracle onset: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte), matching “Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it! It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he will be saved out of it.” (web:Jer.30.7) — an exclamation over the day's own severity rather than a pronounced judgment against a named party, closing already on the promise of rescue rather than on threat alone. Jacob's name in this same verse carries the defective spelling these bytes attest. A day-formula turn follows at verse 8 without any addressee change, וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא יַעַבְדוּ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte), matching “It will come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds. Strangers will no more make them their bondservants;” (web:Jer.30.8); a full neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack sits inside this same verse, corroborating rather than opening a fresh unit, since no koh-amar or addressee shift accompanies it. The rescue promise continues through the same defective spelling of Jacob's name twice over, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte), matching “Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.30.10). It closes on כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte), matching “For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.30.11). A second fresh koh-amar turns the address to a feminine-singular figure at verse 12, and this row stops there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 8's own bayom-hahu turn to the broken yoke was considered, since it introduces a distinct image from the fear-cry that opens the unit; it is rejected because no koh-amar, addressee change, or discourse imperative marks that specific turn, only the corroborating neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack already carried inside the same verse.

boundary_rationale: The address turns to a feminine-singular figure under a fresh koh-amar, כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte), matching “Your hurt is incurable. Your wound is grievous.” (web:Jer.30.12) — an accusation-shaped wound complaint distinct in addressee from the collective ‘Jacob’/‘Israel’ material just closed. The complaint continues, naming the cause directly, מַה תִּזְעַק֙ עַל שִׁבְרֵ֔ךְ אָנ֖וּשׁ מַכְאֹבֵ֑ךְ עַ֣ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֗ךְ עָֽצְמוּ֙ חַטֹּאתַ֔יִךְ עָשִׂ֥יתִי אֵ֖לֶּה לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.15, byte), matching “Why do you cry over your injury? Your pain is incurable. For the greatness of your iniquity, because your sins have increased, I have done these things to you.” (web:Jer.30.15); a paseq falls in this same verse. It closes on the reversal itself and the figure's own name, כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִדָּחָה֙ קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֔ךְ צִיּ֣וֹן הִ֔יא דֹּרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte), matching “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’” (web:Jer.30.17) — Zion, named outright as the one this wound-and-healing address concerns. A third fresh koh-amar turns the address to Jacob's tents at verse 18, and this row does not reach past that turn.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 12 through 16 alone as a judgment_oracle was considered, since the wound and iniquity language there is accusatory in shape; it is rejected because the unit's own close at verse 17 resolves unambiguously into healing and restoration with no fresh formula dividing the complaint from the reversal it sets up.
literature_type_guess: incurable-wound complaint reversed into a healing promise

boundary_rationale: The address turns again under a fresh koh-amar, now to Jacob's tents rather than the feminine-singular figure just addressed, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי שָׁב֙ שְׁבוּת֙ אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו אֲרַחֵ֑ם וְנִבְנְתָ֥ה עִיר֙ עַל תִּלָּ֔הּ וְאַרְמ֖וֹן עַל מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ יֵשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte), matching “Behold, I will reverse the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. The city will be built on its own hill, and the palace will be inhabited in its own place.” (web:Jer.30.18) — Jacob's name in this same verse carries the PLENE spelling these bytes attest (an added vav before the final letter), contrasted with the defective spelling attested twice over at verse 10 and once at verse 7 within this same range. The covenant formula follows without any addressee change, וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte), matching “You shall be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Jer.30.22); a setumah falls in this same verse. A wrath-storm coda follows, still the same speaker and audience, לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה עַד עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), matching “The fierce anger of Yahweh will not return until he has accomplished, and until he has performed the intentions of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it.” (web:Jer.30.24); a paseq also falls at oshb:Jer.30.23. The unit closes on a hinge verse that restates the covenant formula in universalized form, בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte), matching “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.” (web:Jer.31.1) — naming all the families of Israel rather than Judah alone. A fresh koh-amar opens a wilderness-scene oracle at verse 2, and this row is held to end just before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening verse 1 as the first verse of the following wilderness-grace oracle (verses 2 through 6) rather than as the close of this one was seriously weighed, since its own temporal opening phrase and its universalized covenant formula both look forward as much as back. It is held here instead because no koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative opens verse 1 itself — the next such onset is the koh-amar that actually begins verse 2 — so under the rule that rows cut only at fresh tier-1 onsets, verse 1 stays with the material it caps rather than the material it precedes; this attachment is held at reduced confidence as one of this range's own genuinely open seam questions.
literature_type_guess: Jacob's-tents restoration oracle with a wrath coda

boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens a wilderness scene, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מָצָ֥א חֵן֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר עַ֖ם שְׂרִ֣ידֵי חָ֑רֶב הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte), matching “The people who survive the sword found favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.” (web:Jer.31.2) — a memory of the exodus wandering rather than the tent-and-city imagery just closed. The same voice continues in direct declaration, מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ עַל כֵּ֖ן מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ חָֽסֶד (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte), matching “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.” (web:Jer.31.3). Rebuilding imagery follows, ע֤וֹד אֶבְנֵךְ֙ וְֽנִבְנֵ֔ית בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֚וֹד תַּעְדִּ֣י תֻפַּ֔יִךְ וְיָצָ֖את בִּמְח֥וֹל מְשַׂחֲקִֽים (oshb:Jer.31.4, byte), matching “I will build you again, and you will be built, O virgin of Israel. You will again be adorned with your tambourines, and will go out in the dances of those who make merry.” (web:Jer.31.4) — virgin Israel, tambourines, dances. It closes on a quoted summons, כִּ֣י יֶשׁ י֔וֹם קָרְא֥וּ נֹצְרִ֖ים בְּהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Jer.31.6, byte), matching “For there will be a day that the watchmen on the hills of Ephraim cry, ‘Arise! Let’s go up to Zion to Yahweh our God.’” (web:Jer.31.6). A fresh koh-amar opens a jubilant call to sing at verse 7, and this row stops there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 3's own shift from a report about the figure to a first-person declaration was weighed, but rejected because no koh-amar, addressee change, or discourse imperative accompanies that shift — the whole verse remains one continuous voice addressed to the same figure opened at verse 2.

boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens a jubilant summons, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה רָנּ֤וּ לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְחָ֔ה וְצַהֲל֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם הַשְׁמִ֤יעוּ הַֽלְלוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הוֹשַׁ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת עַמְּךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.7, byte), matching “Sing with gladness for Jacob, and shout for the chief of the nations. Publish, praise, and say, ‘Yahweh, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’” (web:Jer.31.7) — a call to sing rather than a scene description; a paseq falls in this same verse. The regathering closes its first movement on kinship language, בִּבְכִ֣י יָבֹ֗אוּ וּֽבְתַחֲנוּנִים֮ אֽוֹבִילֵם֒ אֽוֹלִיכֵם֙ אֶל נַ֣חֲלֵי מַ֔יִם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יָשָׁ֔ר לֹ֥א יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ בָּ֑הּ כִּֽי הָיִ֤יתִי לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאָ֔ב וְאֶפְרַ֖יִם בְּכֹ֥רִי הֽוּא (oshb:Jer.31.9, byte), matching “They will come with weeping. I will lead them with petitions. I will cause them to walk by rivers of waters, in a straight way in which they won’t stumble; for I am a father to Israel. Ephraim is my firstborn.” (web:Jer.31.9) — Ephraim named as firstborn.
